stem: A research lab's data platform must grow smoothly as its dataset expands: an EC2-attached volume backing an application's working set, and a migration pipeline that keeps moving new instrument output from campus storage into AWS as it is produced. Which TWO capabilities let each of these scale without a forklift replacement? (Select TWO.)

choices.text: Local instance store volumes, adding more local disks as the dataset grows
S3 Transfer Acceleration enabled for the pipeline's uploads to cut per-transfer latency
Amazon EBS Elastic Volumes, increasing size and IOPS on the attached volume without downtime
A single Amazon S3 key prefix handling all of the pipeline's growing request volume
AWS DataSync, scaling by running more tasks and agents in parallel

rationale: Elastic Volumes let you increase an attached volume's size, change its type, or raise its provisioned IOPS and throughput live with no downtime, matching the working-set volume's need to grow in place. DataSync scales a migration pipeline by running more tasks or adding agents in parallel rather than by ordering a bigger physical device, matching the instrument-output pipeline. Instance store volumes are physically fixed to the instance type chosen at launch and cannot be grown or resized, and their data does not survive an instance stop. S3 Transfer Acceleration reduces the distance-driven latency of an individual upload; it adds no parallel transfer capacity to a growing migration pipeline the way running more DataSync tasks or agents does. A single key prefix has a documented request-rate ceiling, so a pipeline whose request volume keeps growing should spread across multiple prefixes rather than staying on one.
